_doc: What joining a call says when it fails, identical on Apple (VoiceFailure.swift) and Android (VoiceFailure.kt). 'messages': the failure code and its one fixed sentence. 'codes': the core's CoreError.Voice code and the failure it is. 'media': signaling worked (or not) by the voice tunnel's counters before and after the attempt ([accepted, up, down, undelivered]); null = no tunnel. No sentence blames a VPN: a phone on cellular hits 'media_blocked' without one. 'gate': the host's voice status, and what the Voice row does.

messages.off: Voice is off on this Skwod right now. Ask the host to check it.
messages.starting: Voice is starting on this Skwod. Try again in a moment.
messages.unreachable: Couldn't reach the host. Check your connection and try again.
messages.no_access: You can't join this channel. Ask the host to let you in.
messages.unavailable: The host didn't open the call. Try again in a moment.
messages.port_taken: Another call is using this device's sound and video path. End it, then try again.
messages.media_blocked: Reached the call, but this device's connection blocked its sound and video. Joining on Wi-Fi may work.
messages.media_silent: Reached the call, but sound and video didn't get through. Try again in a moment.
messages.other: Couldn't join the call. Try again.

media.why: the call server was never reached
packets from an earlier call do not count
signaling worked, the engine could not send to the device's own address
answers came and none could be handed over (a socket on a point-to-point interface)
sent, and the host answered nothing: not this device
both ways and still no call
some answers undeliverable, some delivered: not blocked
the connection was replaced meanwhile (counters went back): nothing is claimed
